analysis.plain_explanation: You have received a legal notice demanding payment for a subscription you cancelled four months ago. Receiving a notice means the company is claiming money, but it is not a court order by itself and does not mean you have automatically lost. You have the right to reply to this notice and explain that you cancelled the service months ago. It is important not to ignore this notice, as deadlines often matter when responding to formal legal demands. Since details of your cancellation and the exact terms of their agreement need careful review, it is best to consult a lawyer or legal aid clinic to help draft a proper reply.

steps.title: (General) Gather and organize all your proofs
steps.detail: Collect the legal notice, your cancellation email showing the date you cancelled, and bank statements showing your payment history. Keep these documents ready to share with a lawyer or legal aid.
steps.where: At home / with your personal documents

steps.title: Contact free legal aid for assistance
steps.detail: Since you received a formal legal notice, you can contact the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) or call the NALSA helpline to get guidance or free legal help to draft a proper reply.
steps.where: District Legal Services Authority or call NALSA helpline 15100

steps.title: Send a formal written reply to the notice
steps.detail: Draft and send a formal reply to the company or the lawyer who sent the notice, clearly explaining that the subscription was already cancelled 4 months ago and attaching your cancellation proof. Do not ignore the notice.
steps.where: By post / registered mail to the opposite party

plan.forum: District Legal Services Authority / Civil Court (if a case is filed later)
plan.summary: You have received a legal notice for Rs 40000 regarding a subscription you cancelled 4 months ago, and you have your cancellation email and bank statements as proof. You should not ignore the notice; instead, you should gather your proofs and consult a legal aid authority or a lawyer to send a formal written reply clarifying that the subscription was already cancelled.

draft_document.text:
To,
[ADVOCATE NAME / SENDER OF NOTICE]
[SENDER ADDRESS]

Subject: Reply to legal notice dated [DATE OF NOTICE] regarding alleged dues of Rs 40000

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing in response to your legal notice dated [DATE OF NOTICE] sent on behalf of [SUBSCRIPTION COMPANY], demanding payment of Rs 40000.

I state that the demand raised in your notice is completely baseless and incorrect. I had already cancelled my subscription with your client 4 months ago, specifically on [DATE OF CANCELLATION], and received a cancellation confirmation email on that date. Furthermore, my bank statements show that no active services have been utilized or paid for since the cancellation.

Since the subscription was lawfully terminated months prior to this demand, I do not owe any amount of Rs 40000 to your client. You are hereby requested to withdraw the said legal notice immediately.

Sincerely,

[YOUR NAME]
[YOUR CONTACT INFORMATION]
